summary: Action-enum dispatch through a virtual call. Reads the object pointer this[1088] (offset 0x1100) whose first dword is a vtable, and invokes vtable entry 37 (offset 0x94) with (this[1088], mappedParam, a3). Maps a2 == 1 to parameter 256, a2 == 2 to parameter 2, and a2 == 4 to parameter 3. Any other a2 returns (a2 - 4) without the vtable call. On the three recognized paths the call result is stored back to this[0] and returned.

local_names.this: dispatcher object holding the result slot at 0x0 and the sub-object pointer at 0x1100
local_names.a2: action enum; recognized values 1, 2 and 4 map to vtable parameters 256, 2 and 3
local_names.a3: pass-through argument forwarded to the vtable call
local_names.result: return value of the vtable call, also stored at this[0]

operations.description: When a2 == 1, call vtable entry +0x94 of the object at this[0x1100] with arguments (this[0x1100], 256, a3)
Else when a2 == 2, call the same vtable entry +0x94 with arguments (this[0x1100], 2, a3)
Otherwise result = a2 - 4; when a2 != 4 return that value immediately without a vtable call and without storing to this[0]
When a2 == 4, call vtable entry +0x94 of the object at this[0x1100] with arguments (this[0x1100], 3, a3)
On the recognized vtable-call paths, store the call result to this[0]
Return the vtable call result on the recognized paths, or (a2 - 4) on the unrecognized path

unresolved: The semantic meaning of the a2 enum values (1, 2, 4) and the mapped vtable parameters (256, 2, 3) is unknown without the vtable object's contract
this[0] is written only on the recognized paths; its role as result/status storage is inferred from the write, not confirmed by a reader
